blocks.md: This lesson follows **Bounding Observation Age** in *Sensor Perception* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Sensor Perception, § Bounding Observation Age
blocks.md: Even when a rack-end observation is dated at capture and placed in a calibrated coordinate frame, the scene it describes belongs to the past. Delivering that measurement across an embodied runtime adds acquisition, bus transport, queueing, and neural inference delay while the robot continues to move. Any delivery deadline for perception must therefore track the full physical interval from energy integration at the detector through dispatch, bounding the observation's age before downstream actuators act.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Observation age matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.

questions.q: The section **Bounding Observation Age** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Observation age runs from the exposure midpoint to dispatch, accumulates stage by stage (exposure, readout, transport, DMA, ISP, backbone, dispatch), and is paid in blind travel that no later stage returns.
Out-of-distribution and input-support monitors flag into the health bitmask and can demote a camera to LiDAR-only operation, but they cannot certify what the transducer itself got wrong.

A measurement is dated at its exposure midpoint or per-point firing time, never at arrival, and rolling-shutter rows and LiDAR sweeps sample the scene at different instants that capture-time geometry must undo.
Spatial error is spent from the same clearance as age, so the clearance inset rests on a measured high quantile of residuals against ground truth, which for stereo grows with range squared.
